label: conj:lifted-crossing-locality
title: Locality of lifted-crossing contributions in the mass expansion
html:
Lifted-crossing locality hypothesis

Conjecture. The joint mass contribution of lifted crossings factorizes into independent local evaluations:

  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{GB}}(\beta\lvert_{S \text{ lifted}})
  \;=\;
  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{GB}}(\mathcal{K}) \cdot
  \prod_{c \in S} \eta(c).

The local factor \eta(c) depends strictly on the individual crossing c, its sign, and the substrate parameter q, completely independent of the broader configuration.

Locality requires that parallel transport of the shape parameter around multiple crossings accumulates zero phase. The Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov connection is flat at every level, because the infinitesimal braid relations that characterise flatness are homogeneous in the coefficients (QOU.Mass.KZFlatnessLevelIndependent); what singles out the physical substrate q_0 is not flatness but semisimplicity of the monodromy target H_n(q_0), which holds because q_0 is not a root of unity. Because q_0 is real and greater than one, a Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov monodromy eigenvalue e^{i\theta} at real level can never equal it; the level is necessarily non-unitary, k + 2 = 2\pi i/\ln q_0 \approx 60.218\, i in the convention q = e^{2\pi i/(k+2)} (Hecke monodromy conjecture). The property fails at roots of unity or at the golden-ratio degeneration threshold, identifying q_0 as the distinguished regime supporting exact exponential mass scaling.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It applies q-deformation identities over an abstract coefficient ring and specializes them to real-valued observables at q_0.
